LESSON: THE ATOM

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: CHEMISTRY FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Inorganic chemistry
Topic 1.2: The Atom
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 24

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers The Atom, part of Inorganic chemistry in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 CHEMISTRY FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How are electrons arranged in an atom?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on The Atom together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: the learner listens keenly and actively using open questions while discussing

with peers the relationship between atomic number, mass number and number of electrons in atoms of elements.

● Digital literacy: the learner continuously learns to use digital platforms with assistive technology while watching or

listening to animations on atomic models, isotopes and electron arrangement of atoms

● Creativity and Imagination: the learner experiments with ideas while modelling the structure of s and p orbitals using

locally available materials.

● Learning to learn: the learner reflects on their own work as they practise illustration of electron arrangements for the

first 20 elements using s and p orbitals

8

Values:
● Social justice: The learner advocates for harmonious relationship in groups while discussing the meaning of isotopes

and relative atomic mass.

● Integrity: The learner shows self-discipline by appropriately using digital devices to watch or listen to animations,

simulations or audio visual video clips on electron arrangement of the atom.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

● Socio-Economic and Environmental issues (Environmental conservation): the learner responsibly uses locally

available materials to model the structure of s and p orbitals using locally available materials.

● Life skills (Self-esteem): the learner gains confidence while presenting findings on the meaning of isotopes and

relative atomic mass.

● Socio-Economic and Environmental issues (global citizenship): the learner brainstorms with peers on the

contributions of scientists in the development of atomic theory/models.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Print and tactile braille version of the periodic table, 3-D models of orbitals and structure of the atom, plasticine, clay,

braille

labelling tape, manilla papers, markers, digitals devices with assistive technology.

Suggested Key Skill(s)

Write the electron arrangement of elements using s and p notation.
